Remembering rejected transport IDs does not implement the promise that cached mis-signed events are not reported again; duplicates still reach say and appendLog.

Cannot verify that the F8 benchmark overlay, its class names, or any caller of this script still exist; no export-index row and no referencing file in the material.
Spending the retry budget does not make the failure non-transient as the MAX_RETRIES comment states; retryDecision preserves the classifier's transient value.
OUTAGE_CHILD_THRESHOLD has an unused public export while remaining the internal outageThreshold default.

stateDeaths has an unused public export; its defensive reader is used only inside the module.

GITHUB_SIDE_JOBS has an unused public export while remaining an active internal classification table read at line 349.

JOBS_MAX_PAGES has an unused public export while remaining moreJobPages' internal pagination default.

The actionable contract still names runner famine as the sole non-actionable cause, but never-started, escalated waiver and Pages-with-empty-blockers also return actionable: false, and the famine branch is below, not above.

A 2026 message dated at the epoch is about 56 years overdue, not fifty-five.
The claimIsOurs doc lists four release paths but says "five copies".

WAKE_REASONS, VERIFICATION_REASONS, pendingAgeMs and RECONNECT_MAX_MS are test-only exports whose behaviour is live internally, so not cruft.

The comment promises the speaker turns before he speaks, but g.rotation.y is assigned at 3446 while yaws.current changes at 3465 immediately before speakWork at 3466, so the rendered turn does not precede the word.

The __placeForceFill doc calls it “the only thing that dips anybody today” and says the errand flips emptyJar to fullJar with no act in between, contradicting 3363–3369 “THE LIVE DIP … The errand's own phase drives it now” and that implementation.

The ErrandVillager comment says the carrier's jar is “the same vessel the task walkers carry”, but TaskWalker uses a closed cylinderGeometry [0.12, 0.16, 0.32, 8] while Jar has different dimensions, an open wall, a separate base and contents.

The TaskWalker's jar is still the closed opaque cylinder, while the Jar section (3656) says the closed cylinder is gone and the ErrandVillager comment (3591) says the carrier's jar is the same vessel the task walkers carry.

The comment says the player has “already seen” this jar in the village, but where there is no well no jar-carrying TaskWalker is mounted (4255 hasWell && homes.length > 1 gate), so the jar has not been seen.
The comment says the rim is FLARED past the body's waist, but JAR_RIM_R=0.155 is smaller than JAR_WAIST_R=0.16.

The JAR_WATER_DROP doc says it also sets the empty jar's hollow depth, but 3715 selects full ? JAR_WATER_DROP : JAR_HOLLOW_DROP and the empty hollow uses the separate, undocumented JAR_HOLLOW_DROP=0.13.

The comment says the meniscus is flattened to a fifth of the jar's height, but its height is (0.155 − 0.008) × 0.65 ≈ 0.0956 m whereas one fifth of JAR_HEIGHT is 0.064 m; the ~6.5 cm clearance claim still matches the code.

The base comment says the base makes the vessel a jar and not a tube, but the base circle radius JAR_BASE_R=0.13 is narrower than the wall's bottom radius JAR_WAIST_R=0.16, leaving an open annular ring.

The meniscus explanation (3699–3701) says an interior disc is edge-on from every standing distance, contradicting 3638–3641 which say the jar's lean (rotation [0.16, 0, 0.1]) lets the water be seen from a standing eye.

The WaterStand doc says it “draws `jars` of them”, but the component has no jars prop (signature { x, z, jarRefs }); it mounts waterStandCapacity hidden jars and the parent frame loop toggles visibility via work.standJars.

The radius prop doc calls it “the children's play area”, but Kids receives playRadius={ground.radius} from the layout's playGround separately from radius in both render branches; radius is the walkable radius for nav and movement.

The missing-playground comment and diagnostic (4075, 4083) promise an origin-centred chase fallback, but !playGround makes bankStage null at 4102 and the Kids gate (!bank || bankStage) at 4204 then suppresses rendering in a village with a bank.

The placement-anchor collection is described as “Every spot this settlement hands out” but reads only homes, villageAdultStations, errands and buildings, omitting ground (Kids) and loom (Loom); the watcher implementation is outside the material.

The comments say the column spans from above the eye to below the feet and is centred on the eye, but fall is mod(RAIN_HEIGHT) in [0, 15) and the group sits at y=EYE=1.5, so streaks run from 1.5 m up to 16.5 m and never below roughly eye height; no downward centring offset is applied.
The comment claims the column follows the head so it always surrounds the player, but line 59 copies only camera x and z and fixes y to EYE=1.5 regardless of camera height.

The Talkers' gestureA/gestureB refs never leave restGesture() in a real run; only the DEV hook writes them and the frame loop never advances them, and the doc says this awaits a user decision (2195–2196, 2234); the doc's start is outside the material.
The FireTender claims to kneel at the fire pit but faces a hard-coded point (-3.5, 2.5) via Math.atan2 instead of the per-layout firePos prop used at 4237.
The TaskWalker comment speaks of another inhabitant “on the way to the field”, but a TaskWalker only walks to the fire (2245) or to the well (2258).
else if (!task) sits directly after if (task), so its condition always holds; a plain else suffices.

Two passages disagree on where the water errand is spoken: 3207–3209 and 3943–3944 place the carrier's word at the head of the water path, 3947 says the errand is ordered at the water stand; which is current lies in the adultWork module outside the material.

The WaterStand doc claims a delivery past the cap replaces the oldest standing jar and that the stand is a low platform beside the fire; neither the adultWork standJars cap logic nor the layout's waterStand placement is in the material to confirm.

speakWork's gesture parameter is typed optional with an early return at 3821, but its only caller (3466) always passes a defined per-villager ref from an array filled to count at 3097; the return would also silence the word, contradicting “the DISTANCE decides all three”.

The bank prop doc describes it only as the ground the children's stage stands on, but bank is also passed to ErrandVillagers (4227) and Walkers (4235) and shapes the nav grid via buildPlaceNavGrid({ radius, bank }) at 2707.

A bare useGame((s) => s.balanceVersion) subscription with no reader of the value follows a comment (4069–4071) explaining the play-ground derivation moved out of this component, so nothing here justifies the re-render.
The presence comment says “the elder and the home vignettes REMAIN” in the away season, but the village render list (4193–4263) mounts no elder; lines 1–2194 are outside the material.

The comment says “the search below it stays as the fallback”, but no search follows in this component; 4116 is a single climbBoulder call and the fallback lives inside climbBoulder, whose body is outside the material.

The comment says every settlement always carries a play ground (layout.ts builds one), while the devAssert at 4079 treats a missing one as a real reportable state and the port branch also consumes the fallback; layout.ts coverage for ports is outside the material.
The comment says the separation assert below “used to accept !playGround outright”, but the assert at 4090 still starts with !playGround ||; the change was an added assert, not a change to that one.
The body-set comment says “one per settlement” twice in two differently worded sentences, which reads like a merge leftover.

The FigurePose | null pose refs in Pounder (2283/2290), Drummer (2386/2402) and ErrandVillagers (3108, 3400/3413/3421/3431) are always initialised non-null and never set to null, so their null guards cannot fire.

The comments cite the travel scene's column width of 55 (“not the travel 55”, header “55 units wide”) as a live comparison; the travel scene's rain radius is outside the material and cannot be confirmed.
The comment likens __placeBodies to __placeTag (“Dev-only, like `__placeTag`”), which is not defined in this chunk; lines 1–2194 and other files are outside the material.
The file summary ("walkable port/village") omits the monument place mode implemented at lines 2483 and 3225–3233 (walkable Giza monument scene).

The FIRE_SHADOW_MAP_SIZE campfire-shadow comment still says "debug toggle, default OFF" and "256 keeps the quality", while lines 1183–1193 make shadows graphics-level-driven (off on low, 256 on medium, 512 with soft edges on high); the actual default is not supplied.
Three consecutive blank lines (214–216) between interactiveLabel and the shared-materials section mark where something was removed; nothing remains in the gap.

The groundDebugFlat flat-material branch is a diagnostic left over from the point-111 WebGPU black-patch hunt and may no longer serve any purpose; whether the debug UI still sets it and whether point 111 is closed is outside the material.
"Every roof number below comes from roofClearance" overstates the shared configuration: the parapet uses literals at 452–453 and roof-label heights use 1.18, 0.5, 1.9 and 1.2 at 512–515.
"the one store write of the whole trip" needs checking against useGame.getState().sendDrumMessage() at line 653, whose mutations cannot be confirmed from the attachment.
Stall's optional default plenty = 1 is unused: its only invocation at 1035 always passes plenty from Dwelling, where the property is required and typed number at 1022.
"Prayer-hall body with a slightly battered profile" precedes an ordinary boxGeometry with no taper or vertex modification.
FirePit's intro presents the cook shelter as unconditional ("under an open-sided thatched COOK-SHELTER"), but line 1256 renders it only when sheltered and 1196–1198 describe unsheltered fires.
FirePit's default blaze = 1 is never selected: the only invocation at 3239 supplies blaze={fireBlaze}, whose initializer at 2495–2506 always returns a number.
FirePit's missing-rainRef branch (rainRef ? rainAmount(...) : 0) is unreachable: the sole caller at 3240 always supplies the ref created by useRef(0) at 2547.

The fallback cook-shelter meshStandardMaterial (thatchMat ? null : ...) appears unused: CookShelter receives FirePit's thatchMat and the sole FirePit caller supplies mats.thatch; createSurfaceMaterial is not attached so an undefined result cannot be ruled out.
"phase ÷ (speed × cadence) is 1" treats accumulated phase as a normalized rate; line 1658 computes phase from time-dependent distance plus the independently randomized it.phase from 1584.
The landscape-backdrop annulus-heightfield doc block (1776–1782) is detached: it is followed by blank lines and the skyline doc/GizaSkyline, while LandscapeBackdrop at 1900 carries no doc.
The Table Mountain doc block (1785–1790) sits directly on top of the Giza doc block and GizaSkyline (1796) and documents nothing; TableMountainSkyline at 1816 has no doc.

The candidate-list doc names pickForKeyPress, which does not appear in the file; the split is done by pressKey (2842) and advanceKeyPicks (3107); whether useKeyTarget still exports that name is outside the material.

The candidate-list doc says "A dig site, the chief's own socket and the rest of the rebuild join this list here", but the chief already joins at 2353–2368 and no dig-site action or candidate exists in UseAction or settlementUseCandidates.
The comment about where the settlement's walls stand and the children's play ground is followed by isPort/isMonument/isVillage flags, which have nothing to do with walls or the play ground.
The monument-ground comment says "desert sand, like a port's ground", contradicting lines 292–295 ("not the port's pebbled sandy earth", monument-only { sand: true }).
The walk-state comment calls eased velocity "all camera/feel only", but lines 3005–3011 use w.velF and w.velS to calculate movement and update the logical player position.
The comment says the touch quality preset (point 84) halves the shadow-map resolution, but line 2557 says the graphics level (point 276) drives it.

The dev-hook cleanup (2649–2656) deletes eight window keys but not __placeSpots (2602) or __chiefHome (2607), so both stay on window after unmount; __chiefHome closes over a walk reset for a scene that is gone.

"A modal dialog freezes looking as it freezes walking" is stronger than the implementation: a dialog zeros movement targets, but 2995–3011 still ease existing velocity and resolve movement, including displacement by the chief.

The speech-guess opener still says it is opened "by the SAME use key" and rejects "a second key", but point 1139 assigned Space to use and E to guessing (2758–2761, separate subscriptions 2832/2862); a real Space press uses only and only the pad keeps both meanings.
The comment contrasts with "the last rendered frame's nearRef", but no nearRef declaration exists anywhere in the file.
"touch and pointer-lock look identical" overstates parity: touch handling at 2970–2971 updates only yaw from dx, while mouse handling at 2702–2710 also updates pitch from movementY.
"a standing camera sits at exactly EYE_HEIGHT" retains an absolute assumption after terrain-relative footing was added; 3079–3080 supply EYE_HEIGHT + footing to placeCameraPose.
Footstep phase claims to "advance by the actual speed" but line 3052 uses Math.hypot(w.velF, w.velS), the eased velocity, not the collision-resolved movement computed at 3007–3011.
The prompt comment retains the old "the key names the HUT ... and the MAN" description, while 3117–3123 implement action labels through chiefPromptLabel (ask, repeat, call back).

The chief's mount JSX comment says "he stands beside his own door for the rest of the run", contradicting the Chief component doc (570–575: walks across to the drummer, stays a minute, walks home) and lines 682–684 which clear chiefOutside on return.
"enterable buildings carry a pulsing marker" mischaracterizes the set: the implementation maps every interactive, including the chief's hut, which 2733–2735 handle as an outside meeting.
The teaching-stone JSX comment (ending 3257) is followed by an empty line and the play-rock comment/PlayRocks; no teaching-stone element is rendered in the scene.

The play-rocks comment says "the same dressing at the same size as the teaching stone", but that stone is no longer rendered and PlayRocks uses buildPlayRock's higher-detail flat-base geometry (1406–1409) at rocks.scale (1428) rather than buildRock's dressing; the former stone's size cannot be established from the attachment.
PlaceLife gets a hard-coded firePos={[-3.5, 2.5]} while the fire itself is drawn at VILLAGE_FIRE (3237), so the two can drift apart; the value of VILLAGE_FIRE in layout is outside the material.

The header's unconditional brief-lifetime claim ("gone again after a moment") omits labels held against expiry while targeted, per lines 115–122 which select the target before pruning because targeting "holds its label against expiry".

The header says "the scene never carries standing text", but PlaceScene draws standing map-label text over buildings (383–385, 521, 722–724) and over the chief (689); the claim should be scoped to speech labels.

The targeting comments (108, 118–119) still describe the speaker pick as "the use-key candidate" and PlaceScene deciding "whether SPACE actually means him" (point 691), but since point 1139 E acts on the speaker (168–173; PlaceScene 2858) and a real Space press uses only, with combined selection reserved for the pad (PlaceScene 2839–2842).
ADULT_CONCEPTS is exported, read only by tests, and never used by the module itself.

AdultPhase (l.43), DigUtterance (l.44) and AdultWorker (l.67) have no importer; only the export keyword is dead, the local types stay. A said remove, B said rewrite (drop export); the more conservative rewrite is given.
AIM_CLEARANCE has no importer; it is only read by siteClear at l.357. A said remove, B said rewrite (drop export); the more conservative rewrite is given.

The header still says RIVER is spoken by the empty-jar carrier setting out (and contrasts it with DIG as an invitation), but the code has a separate sender speak RIVER as the order and the carrier report back.
The header promises the two digging situations use different sites, but digSiteFor picks the first free clear site from a rotating start with no exclusion of the other situation's site.
The sender description says he walks nowhere, but he is assigned senderSpot with arrived=false and readyWord waits for his arrival.
anotherFreeAdult describes selecting the stationary sender, but its caller assigns the result to the travelling carrier.
Two stacked casting comments disagree on whether the stand is the carrier's spot; the code gives both adults separate surrounding spots, so the first comment is superseded.

The frame-deferral comment claims an unconditional one-word-per-frame limit, but urgent requests bypass it and l.159-160 document several emissions before a kill.

The final arrived-walk cleanup branch (owes nothing, no hold) is unreachable through this module's own transitions and bypasses clearPair's floor release. A said remove, B said file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.
The worker role variant is never assigned or tested by this module; every constructor assigns initiator or partner.
via is set to null by every task constructor and never assigned a waypoint here, so goalOf's fallback and the !t.via guard only ever see null.
waterHead is declared in the geography but never read here; casting and travel use waterFoot, waterFill and waterStand.
AdultWorkConfig.dwellSeconds (and per B also pace) is never read by the module that declares the config.
The promise to record every completed stroke exceeds the accounting: digStrikeCrossed returns a boolean and strikes increments once per dt even across multiple cycle boundaries.
The comment says the report's aim is replaced by the sender's position, but say.aim for water-back is never read; readyWord builds its aim from sender.x/z.
The hushed flag is written in five places but never read in this file; the only documented reader is the removed blanket exemption.
AdultWorkState is imported only by tests but is the return type of createAdultWork, used in 8 files, so it is live.

AnimalAnchor (l.30), AnimalBody (l.39) and AnimalPen (l.46) have no importer; only the export keyword is dead, the local interfaces stay. A said remove, B said rewrite (drop export); the more conservative rewrite is given.
ANIMAL_RADIUS is imported only by tests but drives nudgeToFree and resolveMove, so it is live.
The arithmetic 0.18 + 0.3 = 0.48 m hard-codes a walker radius of 0.3 that this file does not define; ANIMAL_RADIUS is WALKER_RADIUS from ./collision.
The promise that final anchors remain inside their pen is not enforced after nudgeToFree replaces the candidate without an enclosure check.
BACKDROP_RIM_DROP has no importer; it is only read inside backdropBase at l.111. A said remove, B said rewrite (drop export); the more conservative rewrite is given.
Comments promise a flush disc-edge join, but l.148 excludes equality from the relief-free span so positive tapered relief is added exactly at the edge.
discHorizonY's explanation says backdrop ground past the edge dips below the disc plane, but backdropSurfaceY clamps relief to nonnegative and the base is 0 past the edge.
panoramaStandY still describes a falling plain being supported by the disc-horizon fallback, but the heightfield past the edge is clamped to at least zero.
The panoramaStandY doc names an old panoramaGroundY clamp that no longer exists anywhere in the chunk.
The disc-horizon alternative is redundant for silhouettes outside the disc viewed from inside: backdropHeightAt is nonnegative and discHorizonY nonpositive, so Math.max always selects own.
backdropTaper and backdropBase docs say they are shared with backdropHeightAt, but backdropHeightAt calls neither and goes through backdropSurfaceY.
backdropBase and PANORAMA_RING_CLEARANCE are imported only by tests but feed live functions in the file.
BackdropMaterialHandle has no importer; it is only the local return type of createBackdropMaterial. A said remove, B said rewrite (drop export); the more conservative rewrite is given.
The header claims the smooth-shading contract is tested in backdrop.test.ts and cites section numbers that differ from those at l.39.

BankConcept (l.68), BankPhase (l.71), BankRole (l.74), BankAim (l.85) and BankRoundConfig (l.261) have no importer; only the export keyword is dead, the local types stay. A said remove, B said rewrite (drop export); the more conservative rewrite is given.

The heading announces THREE wrong readings but only two bullets (ROCK, river current) follow; the missing third cannot be reconstructed from the supplied material. A said file-point, B said rewrite; the more conservative file-point is given.
The off-game boulder teaching is described as mandatory and never optional, but overtime abandonment at l.1242-1243 and the corroboration wording at l.1241 permit abandoning it.

The header and openCycle helper docs promise a RIVER call at every cycle opening, but openCycle gates the call on rockKnown. A said rewrite, B said file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.
The introduction says every run announces a direction, but rock-only runs call openRun directly without an announcement.
The introduction and openRun doc promise a tap on every run, but l.1063-1068 allow a silent run when contact cannot be reached.

The introduction promises every child reaching the far rock calls ROCK, but arrival is registered by reachDistance while speech requires a reachable stand, approach and contact that can be discarded silently.
The quarry field comment says the target is held for the run, but stepRun re-runs chooseQuarry every frame and switches beyond targetSwitchMargin.
direction is documented as null outside the run phase, but announceRun assigns it while the game is still in gather or regroup.
The pending-field description presents speech-gap omission as universal, overlooking speech-floor deferral which retains the teaching moment.
The tapFor comment says a silent opening holds nobody, but openRun always sets returnFor and stepTapReturn still holds the other children.
abandonedBoulder does not guarantee the guard ended without a naming: overtime sets the flag without clearing the climber, and stepClimb can still emit ROCK afterwards.
The climb is not bounded solely by its three stage lengths: l.552 can wait indefinitely for maySpeak and descent may last four times climbSinkSeconds.
openRoam's doc says a climber is picked, but openRoam resets s.climber to -1 and stepRoam performs the pick.
roamGoal promises a heading the child has not just come from, but the code draws a uniform random heading with no exclusion.
stationAt's description says a group of four forms one line, but the code arranges rows of three with slot 3 in a second row.
The run-end comment equates safety with touching the far rock, but arrived is set on entering reachDistance before contact.
Walking between runs is not the only time tagged children move; stepPart converts out children to catchers and walks them toward stage.roam.
Separation and placement comments keep a fixed half-metre climbing height, but lift is derived from boulder.height and the ascent/descent fraction.
The phase-order rationale cites a no-utterance-slows-a-child criterion incompatible with the deliberate group holds for the spoken tap.
playing is set true once and never set false in this module, so every if (s.playing) test is always taken; external writers not supplied.
The speech-watch doc refers to a five-word rebuild while the header and BankConcept type describe four words.
The header's list of utterance moments omits the boulder moment present in BankMoment.
A stranded JSDoc above stepBankGame's own JSDoc describes advanceBankGame, which has no doc.
The doc says the watch is DEV-gated at the call site, but the import.meta.env.DEV gate sits inside stepBankGame itself.
'picked HERE rather than only when a roaming phase opens' implies the climber is also picked at phase open, which no longer happens.
'the bound below' refers to the roam overtime bound, which lives in advanceBankGame above stepRoam.
landingFor says the per-frame re-read is above, but it is in stepClimb after this function.
tapReturnSeconds is documented as a settling radius but is a time; the settling radius is catcherStationDistance.
A bare block inside the catcher loop is the leftover of a removed loop or condition, and s.children[ri] is read before the ri < 0 check.
Two in-file statements about the boulder stand's length disagree (seven seconds vs 2.8 s); the balance value is outside the material.
A comment hard-codes the station arrival radius as 1.3 m, but the value comes from cfg.reachDistance.
A comment quotes a measured 92 % naming rate against the balance file; the current balance and measurement are outside the material.
wayTo claims the adults' errands follow the same planning rule, but adultWork has no route planning here since via is always null.
wordToward and ClimbStage are imported only by tests but are used live in the file.
The boundary introduction and LUT explanation keep the waterline as the lobe's endpoint, but the lobe extends past it to bank.wadeEdge.
'A kilobyte of lookup' understates the Float32Array of 1024 entries, which is 4096 bytes.
maxBoundaryRadius's claimed maximum at the plateau angle can be exceeded inside the smooth fade, where the 1/cos radius still rises; imported angle values not supplied.
The cos <= 1e-6 guard after the fade-angle early return is unreachable whenever BANK_FADE_ANGLE is below pi/2.

The doc says walking-out answers nothing anywhere, but non-drum villages return 'no-message' for every non-in-hut phase; reachability of walking-out there is not supplied. A said rewrite, B said file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.
The header confines the drummer's CHIEF naming to the Bambara paragraph and says the head man elsewhere only acknowledges, but the code has the drummer name the chief in every village while in-hut.

ChiefWalkTiming (line 34) and ChiefStep (line 44) are exported but no other file imports them; they are used only as parameter/return types in this file. A proposes dropping the export, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.
chiefIsOutside is exported and used only by tests; no production caller and no internal use.
DRUMMER_LOOKS_AT is exported but no other file imports it; its only live use is inside drummerFacing in this file, so the export can be dropped.
The description of a clear, measured walking line conflicts with the documented maasai-village exception where a collider sits on the line and he brushes through it.
The frame-rate independence claim omits the one-transition-per-call limitation: a long walking-out tick returns at-drummer even when enough time elapsed for the stay and return.
The comment says PlaceLife draws the drummer with exactly this point's yaw, but PlaceLife never imports the constant; the yaw reaches it through drummerFacing.
The comment says both drum shells reach no further than 0.5 m out, but the drum geometry in drummerPose.ts reaches about 0.62 m sideways and 0.78 m forward.
The comment says at his own door he faces the open ground again, but in-hut returns the same standingFacing yaw as at the drummer, and no figure is drawn while he is in the hut.
A dated OPEN finding (sweep over 22 villages, maasai-village collider 0.24 m into his footprint) is embedded as // lines inside a JSDoc block; its numbers are an unverified snapshot.
The header narrates removed behaviour ("does not speak at his own door any more") instead of describing the current behaviour.
The chief's-labels speaker id sits beside prose saying he no longer speaks; which labels still use the id is not visible in the material.

CircleCollider (tests only), BoxCollider (line 19) and SegmentCollider (line 39) are exported without production importers; all are needed only as members of the Collider union. A proposes dropping the exports, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The small-distance box branch labelled "Exactly on the surface" handles points just outside the surface; exact boundary coordinates enter the earlier branch at line 81.
The dead-centre fallback says it pushes toward the place origin, but the code adds a positive multiple of the position vector, pushing away from the origin.
The circle fallback's extra zero-length fallback is redundant: ox becomes 1 when both coordinates are zero, otherwise hypot is already positive.
The claimed exit along a segment's left normal does not cover a zero-length segment, where ex = ez = 0 and the point is returned unchanged despite overlap.
The claim that radius/2 sampling cannot step over a collider conflicts with inhabitantBodies.ts:265-269, which explains near-tangent chords can be shorter than any sampling gap.
A clear sampled endpoint does not establish an unobstructed escape route; hasEscapeDirection tests only offset endpoints, never the intervening segment.
tryNudgeToFree, nudgeWhere and nudgeToFree describe "nearest" points, but the implementation returns the first accepted angular sample on successive rings.
nudgeWhere claims to return a spot the caller calls free, but on failure it returns the rejected original position with found: false.
The file header lists only circles and oriented boxes, but the module also resolves segment (wall-panel) colliders.
nudgeToFree is described as serving only the layout builder, but ten other files use it, gizaSite.ts among them.
The "Spawn freedom (point 155)" section header now also covers PLAYER_RADIUS and CHIEF_BODY_RADIUS, which are unrelated to spawn freedom.

DigSiteAppearance (line 3) and DigSiteFurniture (line 25) are exported with no importers; they are only local return types. A proposes dropping the exports, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.

The claim that the last ring sits exactly where the height reaches zero ignores the 0.004 offset added at line 48 and depends on spoilHeightAt/SPOIL_RADIUS in placeGround.ts, which is not supplied. A proposes rewrite, B proposes file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.
The comment refers to "this point" without naming a work-order, so the reference has no subject.

DrumStroke (line 96) and DrummerPoseFrame (line 206) are exported with no importers; their local type uses remain live. A proposes dropping the exports, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.

drumHandPoint is exported only for tests and nothing in the file calls it; drummerPoseAt uses drumHandPose instead. A proposes remove, B proposes file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.
The header and DRUMMER_LEAN say the trunk tips about the hip, but lines 119-120 say the legless figure rotates about the ground and line 128 passes pivot 0.

The comments say the bearing puts the hand on the drum's own axis and the stroke follows the drum's position, but the solve matches only drum.x and never reads drum.z. A proposes file-point, B proposes rewrite; the more conservative file-point is given.
The quoted lean displacement (0.05 m down, 0.08 m forward) was stated for a hip pivot; with the ground pivot the lever arm is longer, so the figures are likely stale.
DRUM_HEAD_DIP, DRUM_STROKE_CLEARANCE, drumHeadTop, drumStroke and drumHandPose are exported only for tests but used internally by drummerPoseAt.
The per-frame pose behaviour doc sits on the DrummerPoseFrame interface while the exported drummerPoseAt function has no doc of its own.
The header narrates the replaced armAim(±0.26, -0.2 + lift) stroke as its opening section.
DrummerVoice is exported with no importers; its local type uses remain necessary. A proposes dropping the export, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.
GizaAmbientAnchor is exported with no importers; its local array annotation remains live. A proposes dropping the export, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The inline comment says a monument site has no inhabitants, while the header and GIZA_AMBIENT place ambient people there.
GIZA_SPAWN_Z is said to spawn the traveller just inside the southern edge, while the same doc says the spawn no longer follows the grown radius.
The comment places a cameleer with his camel by the Sphinx, but the cameleer anchor is about 20 m south and the camel near the Sphinx stands alone.
"~52°" holds only for the edge of a four-sided cone with height 1.28 × circumradius; that shape's face slope is about 61°, while the real Giza face is about 52°.
The doc cites measurement figures (340, 191, 76, 720 azimuths, ~27 m) that live in gizaSite.test.ts, outside the material.
GIZA_SPAWN_Z and GIZA_SLOPE are exported only for tests but are used internally at lines 93 and 179.

GrassTuft (line 16) and GrassScatterInput (line 18) are exported with no importers; their local uses in scatterGrassTufts remain live. A proposes dropping the exports, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The header says tufts cover the walkable ground, but the scatter radius extends up to 12 m past the walkable radius.
The comment says ports get a sandier cover, but this module only changes the tuft count; tuft colouring lives elsewhere.

SeparationConfig (tests only) and SeparationWorld (line 125, no importers) are exported parameter types of widely used exports; local uses remain live. A proposes dropping the export, B proposes keep; the more conservative keep is given.
separateAll is used only by tests, has no internal use, and its doc names a whole-set-owning caller that does not exist.
The nudges field describes successful pickups, but lines 431-433 count every nudge attempt whether or not free ground was found.
groundOccupied documents a moverRadius parameter; the actual parameter is moverBodyRadius at line 213.
The occupancy radius is not the exact threshold at which separation starts correcting; pushBody skips distances at or above min - cfg.slop.
stepRoundBodies still describes endpoint-only triggering and a single groundOccupied probe, but the gate at line 299 is a continuous segment test (crosses) over all bodies.
The wedged counter is not a general timer for unresolved overlap; opposing overlap vectors can cancel and lines 393-396 reset wedged despite remaining overlaps.
The movement-result docs omit displacement from a successful escape teleport; lines 427-429 can move the body before returning 0, so separateBody reports false.
The promise of nudging to free ground in bounded time omits that world.nudge is optional and the body moves only when it exists and returns found: true.
The stiffness no-overshoot claim is not guaranteed for multiple overlapping neighbours, since full overlap vectors are summed before stiffness is applied.
The stiffness knob still scales the push by a fraction while the header says the fractional correction was replaced by taking the whole overlap.
The private pushBody function has unused default initializers for world and budget; both calls supply the arguments explicitly.
separateBody is still described as damped, but the damping was removed and the whole overlap is taken.
The comment refers to a rejection "below" that no longer exists; the deflectedStep result is returned directly.
"FULLY BOXED IN, THE ORIGIN COMES BACK" holds only if deflectedStep returns the origin when every bearing fails; local code returns the origin only for a zero-length step.
The header cites a five-behaviours list and measured figures (192-537 pair-frames, 1.2 m/s, shipped 8 m/s) that live outside the file.
LanePoint is an exported interface used nowhere, not even in this file, which uses coordinate tuples throughout.

bendAround claims to iterate until the whole polyline clears the obstacle, but the loop is capped at six insertions, allows 0.05 m slack, and later obstacles can move points without rechecking earlier ones.
LaneSlot.anchor is the originating sample on a segment, not necessarily the closest point on the entire lane centreline.
The PLACE_RADIUS doc claims the factor alone moves the whole settlement, but ports use an unscaled radius (30 + size * 6 at :899) and many village distances are hard-coded literals that do not scale.
The door-field comment still says touching the door opens the building, while :448-449 say only the discrete press enters.
The rocks-field comment calls every scattered rock solid and collidable, but walkable stones (:2086-2090) have their colliders skipped at :2099.
The first waterPath doc block says both carriers speak at the head, while the waterStand docs (:167-169, :303-311) say both words moved to the stand.
The waterPath field carries two stacked doc comments; the first (work-order 688, two-field {head, foot} shape) is superseded by the second (1087).
The second waterPath doc block also keeps the obsolete head-as-speech-location wording, conflicting with the water-stand description at :167-169 and :303-311.
The playGround field is documented as null outside villages, but childPlayGround is called for ports too (:1845-1855) and always returns a PlayGround.
The dig-site anchor doc names a compound wall, but the code measures distance to dwelling centres minus d.r (:2523-2524, :2541).
The doc says WATER_STAND_WORK_RING is restated because layout must not depend on the errand module, yet :35 already imports WORK_ARRIVE_RADIUS from ./adultWork.
The doc claims layout.test.ts pins the two constants together, but the harness header says that test's subjects were split into their own files (1178).

The WATER_PATH_HEAD_RADIUS doc still calls the head the point both carriers speak at (words moved to the stand, :303-311) and says it stands on the bank's bearing, while findHeadHere sweeps from the foot's bearing (:1957).
The 15 m head beyond a 7-14 m compound ring no longer matches compound placement, which starts at 13.5 + rand() * 4 (:1463) plus enclosure radius.
WATER_PATH_HEAD_SWEEP is exported with no outside importer; only findHeadHere at :1963 uses it.
The default dwelling-collider fallback is unreachable: every DwellingKind outside box/warehouse/mosque has a DWELLING_BODY function, so dwellingCircleRadius cannot return null there.
dwellingRoofStandOff is exported with no outside consumer; only :393 and :1129 call it.
chiefStandingSpot defaults hutRadius to 3.35, while the chief hut's collider is interactiveCircleRadius('chief', style), which can be larger; whether callers pass the radius is outside the material.
nearestActionable is used only by tests; the live key press arbitrates over doorCandidates instead.
The nearestActionable doc says the key press acts on this function, but the press now arbitrates over doorCandidates (point 691).
COMPOUND_WALL_GAP and COMPOUND_RING_CORRIDOR are exported with no outside importer; only the compound plan and top-up use them (:1459, :1468, :1477, :1534).
FencePanel is exported but never imported by name; it only types the return of fencePanels. A proposes dropping export, B keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The procedural-layout overview doc block is stranded above isOnLane's own doc; it describes buildLayout (:881), which has no doc of its own.
The exported builtFabric adapter is used only by tests; buildLayout calls fabricOf directly at :1854. A proposes file-point, B keep or file-point; the more conservative keep is given.

The continuous-corridor JSDoc is stranded above PLAZA_CENTRE; its subject clearCorridor at :810 has its own doc and accepts other sample sizes. A proposes rewrite, B remove or merge; the more conservative rewrite is given.
The claim that coarser sampling can only reject more corridors is unproven: :812-818 change both sample positions and clearance with sample, so tested regions are not necessarily nested.

The introductory comment says the water path is laid HERE before a single hut and where BOTH carriers speak, but the lane is searched and pushed at :1931-2014 (laid last per :1916) and speech moved to the stand (:303-311).
The initial waterPath.head coordinates are never read; findHeadHere uses only foot, and head is overwritten at :2013 or the path nulled at :2005.
The comment sends the reader to riverBank.ts for the play rocks' numbers and measurement, but they are documented in this file at :219-258.
The hutDoor comment says the door sits outside the hut collider (r 3.35), but the same offset serves the market (body 2.9) and the real collider is the roof-dependent interactiveCircleRadius.
The zero-distance chief-to-market direction fallbacks are unreachable: chief Z is -14.5 to -11.5 and the nearest market band is -7 to -5, so dChief > 1e-6 always holds.
Two discarded rand() draws remain for the retired village elder so tested layouts stay unchanged; they still advance generator state.
The comment names the spawn corridor as z>6, while the guard at :1037 uses z > 5.
The fixed walk-out zone disc at (0,18) predates pickWayOut (688) and may be legacy; the same literal recurs in the port slot filter at :1206.

The comment says the window gap is measured against body radius, but the check hard-codes 3.2/2.9/3.35 while real village colliders use interactiveCircleRadius, which can grow with roof stand-off; the literals recur at :1328.
The local isFree door check keeps a no-door alternative that none of this builder's interactives can take; all are created with doors (:943, :988, :1226-1230).
The door-seat explanation says stand-off less 0.2 m of air, but the code uses standOff - 0.3 and doorAt adds 0.5 to reach the final 0.2 m clearance.
The alley-presence guard is redundant whenever size >= 3, since the preceding loop pushes an alley for every i < size - 1.
The port market-presence guard's absent-market branch is unreachable: the fixed roster includes market (:1197) and every item is pushed (:1224-1232).
The fire path hard-codes the fire position [-3.5, 2.5] instead of reading VILLAGE_FIRE, whose doc promises a single shared spot.
The hut-body null fallback cannot occur: kind is fixed to 'hut' and DWELLING_BODY.hut exists, so dwellingCircleRadius(...) ?? r always takes the first operand.
The compound dressing comment promises a shed and a drying rack, but the loop (:1548-1554) places only sheds, up to two.
The scatter-plan description says there are no lanes, but :1346-1348 add exit, chief and fire paths and placement checks onLane at :1573.
The LOOSE DRESSING KEEPS ITS DISTANCE block sits above the fence-post pulling loop; the rule it describes lives in clearOfDressing at :2035.
The fence-cleanup explanation refers to a Tuareg camp windbreak, but the scatter plan builds a closed thornbrush goat pen with a gate (:1580-1582).
The collision-set header says every solid object becomes circles, but the set includes oriented boxes (:1712), fence segments and the warp segment (:2484-2490).
The loom-clearance introduction says dwellings stand where the plan put them, but work-order 1191 lets whole households give way (:2253-2259, :2417-2424).
The nominal-loom reservation comment says lifeSpots and villageLifeFootprints both carry the loom, but VILLAGE_SPOTS contains no loom; only the footprints include it.
The statement that children are fixed first and adults move omits the water stand, placed before the quarter (:1778-1779) and entered into the search set at :1826.
The comment speaks of three work sites, but only two dig sites are placed (:2598-2605).
The playGround null guards (:1859, :1870, :1907, :2122) cannot fire because childPlayGround never returns null.
The comment says toChildren is one function for both adult places, but it serves the water head, the dig sites and the loom (:1969, :2575, :2381).
The water path is no longer laid last of all the adults' places; loom placement follows at :2228 and dig sites at :2506.

The water-path description misstates its sweep origin (bearing derived from the foot at :1957) and its earshot check: it is only tested at the candidate head, and inPlayEarshot measures against the quarter, both play rocks and the descent, not the quarter alone.
The comment lists the lanes among what the way out is read off, but pickWayOut reads only colliders (:2023) and lanes carry no collider (:1814).
A standalone historical comment block with no code under it explains the removed waterline collider (work-order 584).
The bank-settling comment still names the water wall among the colliders, though :2141-2147 say the waterline panel was removed and boundary handling replaced it.
Inside if (bank), the absent-play-rock alternatives are unreachable: playRocks and playRockColliders exist exactly when bank does (:907-909, :1749-1752).
The comment says settling moves nothing in any river layout, while :2191-2193 report a 0.9 m move in the first stage.
Surviving water paths cannot lack their search callbacks (:1976-1977) or their inserted lane (:2014) at revalidation; the null guards at :2195 and :2203 are unreachable.
A loose comment about the ground a station may take sits above the displacedBy JSDoc; its subject standingSolids/standingLanes is defined at :2338-2340.
The comment cites a way-out floor (point 688), but the floors are DRESSING_MIN_* documented under work-order 1191; 688 defines no such floor.
The comment says the plaza corridor is a metre to each side; that depends on the imported PLAZA_SIGHT_HALF_WIDTH, whose value in loom.ts is outside the material.
The rebuilding guard redundantly rechecks loom and displaced.line, already established by asked (:2403), displaced (:2404) and the check at :2413.
The ground-work introduction promises three patches (pit, post hole and patch), but the code places a pit OR a post hole plus one patch (:2598-2607).
The claim that the field patch lies beyond the last compound is stronger than the rule; belongs.patch (:2546) checks only radius * DIG_SITE_FIELD_BAND.
The pen field is documented as kraal-only, but the Tuareg scatter camp also sets a goat pen (:1579-1582).

PLACE_RADIUS_BASE, PLAY_ROCK_SPAN, CENTRAL_GROUND_RADIUS, DIG_SITE_*, WAY_OUT_*, WATER_STAND_WORK_RING, WATER_STAND_RADIUS, WATER_PATH_HEAD_RADII, WATER_PATH_WIDTH, DOOR_TRIGGER_RADIUS and COMPOUND_RING_MIN are flagged onlyTests but each drives shipped code inside layout.ts.
The header says the harness is test-only, yet the index does not flag SEEDS, PORTS, VILLAGES, bodyR and Body onlyTests; which non-test files import it is outside the material.
The cache rationale says buildLayout reads nothing but its two arguments, yet it reads module-level balance, world geography, region styles and village plans.
bodyR and interactiveR describe building bodies with pre-roof radii, while layout.ts collides with dwellingCircleRadius/boxes and interactiveCircleRadius.
The if (r > 0) guard can never fail, because interactiveR returns only 3.2, 2.9 or 3.35. A proposes rewrite, B remove; the more conservative rewrite is given.
The header says the layout builder keeps its colliders in PlaceScene, but layout.ts was extracted from the scene.
inwardStationBody is exported with no outside consumer; only weaverStance and villageLifeFootprints use it.
The villageHasWell doc says RIVER is taught on the water path (point 1087), but under 1087 layout.ts moved both words to the water stand (:303-311).
The doc says errand walkers are deliberately not in the station list, yet it includes the water-carrier's and bundle-carrier's stops (:104, :115).
The footprint comment calls every included figure position actual, but the weaver entry via weaverStance() is only a nominal reservation (:28-30).
Fabric proximity is documented as distance to a wall (:159, :180, :291) but computed as distance to building centres (:294).
The MIN_FABRIC doc presents an absolute eligibility threshold, but :376-380 fall back to separated or last-resort ground below it.

The MIN_FABRIC doc attributes the sparsest villages to the scattered forest plans, but the forest plan is street (Congo basin) and scatter is the dispersed camp; design.md §4.5 is outside the material.
The openness and rank-one commentary promise separation is never given up (:204-205, :341-344), but :357-374 let separation give way for fabric.
SEARCH_STEP is described as controlling metre spacing along bearings, but angles use k / bearings * 2π, giving distance-dependent spacing.
The playground rationale says village vignettes move with people-specific layouts, but villageAdultStations uses fixed VILLAGE_SPOTS, LOOM_SPOT and VILLAGE_FIRE offsets.
The unconditional SPECTATOR_MARGIN guarantee is not enforced: rMax (:270) can equal walkRadius and :319 clamps centre distance to zero without shrinking the disc.
The documented first rank omits the MIN_OPENNESS threshold and its preferred subrank at :350-355.
The claim that score decides within every rank omits rank two's primary clearance ordering (:364, :368); score only breaks ties at that clearance.
Entering rank two does not establish that no separated candidate meets the fabric threshold; :355 checks fabric only on the top-scoring separated candidate.
LoomGeometry is exported but imported by no other file; it is used only inside loom.ts (loomAround, LoomPlacement) — drop the export, keep the interface.

LoomPlacement is exported but imported by no other file; it is used only in-file (stationGround, stationHolds, placeLoom's parameter type). A proposed rewrite (drop export), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
WEAVER_SIDE_OFFSET's doc says the distance equals loomWork's WARP_REACH, but WEAVER_SIDE_OFFSET is 0.36 while loomWork.ts:382 sets WARP_REACH to 0.28.
The bankless-station description promises helper tending that the supplied state machine never starts (owed work only when view.teaches, errands only after an allowed word).
The inland-limit comment describes a stricter limit than the implementation, which permits nominalWaterOff + PLAZA_INLAND_SLACK (4).
The separation check samples only weaver, upstream and downstream rather than holding the whole station to the stated distance.

The comment says the water must stay visible as the helper walks out along the warp, but the code sight-tests only station.weaver and station.helperHome, never station.tend or the walk between stands.
The plaza-search description overstates its guarantee of taking the widest available view or proving no suitable ground exists; the sweep is coarse and capped by PLAZA_SWEEP_VIEWED_SEATS=120.
The comment says the giving-way pass's widest seat is a fallback for the first pass's, but widest is recorded only when q === p, i.e. never outside the first pass.
Candidates are not ordered nearest-the-nominal-spot first; radii are exhausted at one bearing before the next bearing is tried.
The 'seldom wider than four inches' historical note needs reconciliation with stripWidth=0.12 m (about 4.72 inches); the source and any intentional enlargement are not supplied.
LOOM_DIRECTIONS is used nowhere, neither in other files nor in this one.

LoomWorkConfig is exported but imported by no other file; it is used only as an in-file type (createLoomWork, nextInterval, stepLoomWork). A proposed rewrite (drop export), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
LoomErrand is exported but imported by no other file; it is used only by LoomWorkState.errand in-file — drop the export, keep the type.
tendWalkSeconds is used nowhere, neither in other files nor in this one.

LoomWorkConfig.helperCycleSeconds is never read: neither createLoomWork nor stepLoomWork consumes it, and loomPicture takes its own default straight from balance.villageLife.loom.helperCycleSeconds (:344). A proposed rewrite, B proposed file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.
The comment says a new station has 'nothing woven', but :140 initializes cloth to rand() * cfg.warpHalf * 0.6.
The documented shuttle phase landmarks (near hand at 0, far side at 0.5) do not match sin(pass * 2π), which is zero at both and peaks at 0.25 and 0.75.
The reed does not beat as the shuttle lands: shuttle extrema fall at phases 0.25 and 0.75 where the beat is zero, and maximum beat occurs at phase 0 with the shuttle centred.
passes is documented as the count since the strip was last taken off, but fold completion (:205-209) clears fold and cloth without resetting state.passes.
The backstop names 'no helper for minutes' as a diagnosable case, but that time is explicitly excluded and owedFor increments only when both view.helper and view.rockHeard are true.
The backstop claims to count only time the word could have been said, yet childrenHear blocks speech at :275 but is absent from the counter condition at :279.
The fallback no longer keeps the tallest stone when no climbable stone exists: :122 excludes every ground-classified stone, so such a scatter returns null.
RINGS is described as distances outside the quarter's rim, but the offsets are applied on top of rim + rock radius + clearance + 1e-3; the historical 110-layout measurements are not supplied.

panoramaDriftVelocity has no production consumer (tests only), and panoramaDriftYaw derives the tangent on its own, so the doc's reason for the export is false. A proposed file-point (tests absent), B proposed remove; the more conservative file-point is given.
The raw-distance gait explanation omits the scale correction the active helper now applies (arc divided by scale at :115).

A free-standing bob-and-nod postmortem describes the removed panoramaGaitBob / panoramaGaitNod, which have no definitions in the module and no code attached. A proposed rewrite, B proposed remove; the more conservative rewrite is given.

DIG_WORK_CLEARANCE is exported but used only in-file (clearOfSpoil's default margin at :82); B adds that DIG_RIM_DISTANCE and clearOfSpoil are exported only for tests. A proposed rewrite (drop export), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
atDigStand checks only an upper distance bound, so it does not establish standing on the working rim or on unbroken ground.
The comment says one bearing step is 30 degrees, but bearings step by Math.PI / 12, which is 15 degrees.
FigureTransform is exported but imported by no other file; it is used only by unplacedInhabitant at :54. A proposed rewrite (drop export), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The blanket no-per-query-allocation claim is not supported: an arrow callback is built for edges.every each query, and a first query per seed builds geometry and triangle objects.
The probe is described as dev-only, but its counters are declared and incremented unconditionally in every build; only the window hook at :183 is gated on import.meta.env.DEV.
Dialog restoration fires on any non-null to null dialog transition, not specifically on a closing activation.

The WallShape (:10), FenceKind (:11) and VillagePlanKind (:31) type exports are imported by no other file; each is used only in-file (RegionPlaceStyle.wallShape, RegionPlaceStyle.fence, VILLAGE_PLANS). A proposed rewrite (drop exports), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The regional styling comments still describe a single settlement arrangement per region (East 'on a ring', South 'loose compounds') despite the mixed plans assigned by people at :60-72.

BANK_SHALLOWS_DEPTH (:75), BANK_BED_DEPTH (:80), BANK_STRETCH_ANGLE_FRAC (:103), bankStretchAngle (:131) and BANK_WATER_PATH_ANGLE_FRAC (:211) are exported but imported by no other file; all are used in-file. A proposed rewrite (drop exports), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The shore is no longer a symmetric 2 × BANK_SHORE_HALF strip with the waterline at its middle; separate top, waterline, shallows and bed rows exist with submerged reaches of 4 and 10 m.
The old instruction that the player stops at the bank top conflicts with the current wading description and the wadeEdge computed from water depth at :519.
BANK_STAND_INSET's reason cites the 'water wall', an invisible collider that work-order 584 removed per :50-65.
The two stretch bearings no longer necessarily lie at the stated fraction of the plateau angle; the fraction is a maximum reduced by bisection when the span exceeds the cap.
The span commentary conflates the bank-point chord (used by spanAt) with the shorter chord between the inset play rocks.

The play-stage measurements (rocks 19.7 m apart, bank points 21.2 m, 3.9 m beyond the upstream rock) predate point 1173's waterline move; the quoted 21.2 m exceeds the current BANK_STRETCH_MAX_SPAN=21 cap, and the fixtures to recheck are not supplied.
The heading says the lane is three walker diameters while its own body says 3.0 m is five 0.6 m diameters (with three as the spec's floor).
The spectator stand is described as set back by the stretch length and off-axis by half, but bankPlayRocksView places it one full length perpendicular to the midpoint with no along-axis displacement.

RockTouch is exported but imported by no other file (used in-file by solveTouch and reachFrom); B adds that touchedPoint is exported only for tests. A proposed rewrite (drop export), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
reachFrom does not return null merely because every candidate is far from contact; it accepts any positive surface radius and keeps the smallest gap without a maximum.

HUT_DOME_WALL_FRACTION (:58), roofLowStripRadius (:176), shedRoofProfile (:225) and cookShelterRoof (:318) are exported but imported by no other file; all are used in-file. A proposed rewrite (drop exports), B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
shedRoofStandOff is used nowhere, so the shed's low-roof collider extension described in the header is not wired. A proposed remove, B proposed file-point; the more conservative file-point is given.

hutRoofStandOff (and per B also placeRoofs, roofHeadroomAt, lowestRoofAt, PlaceRoof, CAMERA_NEAR_REACH) are exported only for tests; the headroom invariant is checked but never used at runtime, and the tests are absent. A proposed file-point, B proposed keep; the more conservative keep is given.
The opening claim that only the low strip becomes non-standable conflicts with the whole-footprint policy at :170-177 for roofs that rise inward (dome, tent).
roofHeadroomAt samples only the eye and twelve equatorial points rather than the minimum over the entire near-plane reach its contract describes.
The promise that a route can never lead onto refused ground conflicts with the permitted final-target exceptions at :219-230 and the appended exact target at :288/:296.
The cell-size explanation treats overlapping footprints at free cell centres as proof the connecting segment is clear, but :95-98 admit collider-clipping steps.
nearestFreeCell returns the first free cell in square-ring traversal order, not necessarily the nearest by distance.
The returned bearing is Math.atan2's principal value, which jumps between +π and −π at the rear seam despite the continuity claim.
The loomAround export is used only by tests; the behaviour is live inside placeLoom (:371, :406).
The waterAhead export is used only by tests; the behaviour is live inside stationHolds (:305).
The PLAZA_SWEEP_VIEWED_SEATS note hard-codes timing measurements and the Bambara plan's 58th seat, which cannot be checked here and will drift.
The warp length is written as a fixed 6 m / six metres (:139, :239) but is 2 × geometry.warpHalf, a calibratable balance value.
stationHolds' docstring lists three checks and omits the inland-slack, walk-radius, water-lane and helper-home sight-line tests.
The comment hard-codes the clearance as 10 m, but the clearance is talk.reach.
placeLoom's docstring describes only the nearest-first fine sweep, which is now the last fallback after up to three plaza passes and the widest-view fallback.

The claim that only a plan with no valid seat reaches the fine sweep is not guaranteed: plaza passes skip seats failing plazaReach, step more coarsely than the sweep, and only the first pass records widest.
The comment says both questions are answered in ONE pass, yet the code runs up to three plazaPass calls.
The block comment covers two passes and never mentions the third plazaViewFar pass added at :424.
The radii array duplicates radiiAt(SEAT_RADIUS_STEP); the two loops differ only by stride.
WEAVER_BODY_RADIUS is documented as the weaver's own body but is also used as the helper's body along his whole walk at :252.
The comment names specific shipped Mandinka plans that cannot be checked here.
warpSign, LoomWorkView and LoomWorkState are exported only for tests; the behaviour they carry is live in-file.
LoomWorkState.clock is incremented at :192 but never read in this file; whether the scene reads it is outside the material.
The header says the reed beats on each arrival (twice per pass), but beats increments once per completed pass and loomPicture's beat peaks only at pass 0/1.
The comment hard-codes the instruction's length as four syllables, but instructionDelay depends on vocabulary.
WARP_REACH's measurement is taken from a KNEELING figure, while loomVisual.ts:7 and loom.ts:40 call the weaver SEATED.
LoomPicture's doc lists only shuttle, beat and cloth, but the interface also carries helper, fold and bundle state.
looseRock re-derives the height inline as ROCK_TOP_UNITS * s next to looseRockTop(s), the very duplication the header says the file exists to end.
deriveClimbRock's JSDoc sits above the RINGS docblock, so it attaches to RINGS while deriveClimbRock at :179 has no doc.
The comment says the bankless default starts due north, but preferred = 0 yields +z, which this codebase maps to south (riverBank.ts:493).

The ring measurements (1.2 m innermost, out to 6.0 m, stopping at 2.4 m) do not line up with RINGS = [0, …, 4.8, 5.6] added to a rim that already includes stone radius + clearance; the clearance value and measurement run are outside the material.
climbBoulder's search fallback cannot run in the shipped game by the file's own claim that every shipped settlement carries a derived stone returned first at :114.
CLIMB_ROCK_TOP is used only by tests and has no in-file use.
panoramaDriftDistance's doc says its raw arc feeds the gait and the render wiring reads it each frame, but :99-101 say the raw arc over-drove the legs and only tests import it.
luminance is documented as a helper for the haze test, but 18 other files use it.
digEarthFlight's doc says clods land on the villagers' walking surface, but the landing height reads only spoilHeightAt, not placeGroundHeight.
The comment says the two immutable meshes are cached, but the cache holds triangle planes keyed by seed after the geometry is disposed.
The comment explains an earlier timer probe using exitPointerLock() that no longer exists.
The comment says refusal signals are diagnostic only, but onRefusal can cancel the intent at :94.
The comment says the three river villages keep their stage exactly where it was, yet the file records the stretch grew from 19.7 m to 26 m and the bank points' 21.2 m exceeds the 21 m cap.
BANK_PLATEAU_ANGLE's example assumes a waterline about 35 m out, a figure that cannot be checked here and predates the raised gap.
bankWaterDepth is used only by tests and nowhere in-file.
BANK_STRETCH_MIN_SPAN is used only by tests and nowhere in-file; its doc says it only makes a test fail.
The header says PlaceScene builds its meshes from the constants here, but most roof constants (GRANARY, TENT_SPREAD, STALL_ROOF, etc.) are module-private.
findPlaceRoute's JSDoc sits above const GOAL_RINGS = 1, so it documents the constant rather than the function at :234.
NAV_CELL and navPointFree are exported only for tests; both are live in-file.
The anchors doc comment ("The object each speaker is drawn as") sits above the numeric `reaches` map; the object map `anchors` is declared two lines later.
updateSpeechTarget still says a LEFT CLICK takes the speaker although the guess moved to its own key (GUESS_KEY_CODE = 'KeyE', useKeyTarget.ts:26–39).

speechTargetLabel/speechUseCandidate still describe SPACE taking the label and nearest-wins arbitration between utterances and doors; keyboard speech now belongs to the guess key and nearest-wins survives only on the pad (useKeyTarget.ts:32–36, 59–70).
forgetSpeechLabel still speaks of the "click target"; the guess is a key press (KeyE).
The `?? reach` fallback and the `reach` parameters of updateSpeechTarget and speechUseCandidate cannot fire: anchors and reaches are always set/deleted together and the anchor check runs first.
pruneSpeechLabels deletes anchors of gone labels but never the matching `reaches` entry, so orphaned reach values accumulate until clearSpeechLabels.
speechTargetLabel is exported but used only by tests; the behaviour is live through speechUseCandidate.

The header still presents a single SPACE candidate list including the utterance as current behaviour; the file's own point-1139 section splits speech onto the guess key with a separate keyboard filter.
